mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds Rate above 5.25% in a given month coincides with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to higher discount rates eroding expected equity payoffs.
regime_hint: Rising inflationary bias in the Fed’s policy framework
failure_condition: Over 60-day rolling window, no significant negative returns coincide with rate hikes (t-test p > 0.05); or FEDFUNDS spikes fail to precede negative 20d SPX moves in 70% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in UNRATE above 5.5% for two consecutive months is associated with a negative 60-day S&P 500 forward return as higher labor-market disengagement raises perceived risk and reduces equity risk appetite.
failure_condition: In a regime where UNRATE is persistently low (<4%), the mechanism produces positive 60d returns; or the 60d return is not statistically different from zero when UNRATE crosses above 5.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both HOUST (industrial production) and GDPC1 (personal consumption) by at least 2% month-over-month predicts a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as it signals robust economic momentum and demand expansion.
failure_condition: In contractionary regimes (e.g., consecutive quarters of negative GDP growth), the interaction fails to predict positive 20d returns (IC < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in INDPRO by more than 3% while HOUST rises by at least 1% indicates supply-side weakness, which is associated with a negative 5-day S&P 500 forward return as market anticipates profit compression.
failure_condition: During periods of robust supply expansion (INDPRO rising >2% while HOUST rising >1%), the mechanism does not produce negative 5d returns (IC > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS remains below 2% for three consecutive months in a non-recessionary regime, the S&P 500 exhibits a positive 60-day forward return as lower policy rates incentivize equity investment.
failure_condition: In a recessionary regime (e.g., negative GDP growth), the policy rate below 2% does not produce positive 60d returns (IC < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden spike in PAYEMS (employment growth) exceeding 50,000 jobs in a month while UNRATE falls below 4% predicts a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as labor market strength offsets rate-sensitive discounting.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 50,000 and UNRATE < 4% in the same month
failure_condition: The interaction fails to predict positive returns when PAYEMS growth is below 20,000 or UNRATE remains above 5% in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in CPIAUCSL (CPI) by 0.5% month-over-month in a deflationary regime is associated with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return as investors anticipate further rate hikes and inflation risk.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL falls by >0.5% from previous month
failure_condition: In inflationary regimes (CPIAUCSL rising >0.2%), the CPI drop does not precede negative 20d returns (IC > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in both INDPRO and RSAFS (retail sales) by at least 1% for two consecutive months predicts a negative 60-day S&P 500 forward return as it signals weak demand and production bottlenecks.
regime_hint: Economic slowdown or soft landing failure
failure_condition: During periods of simultaneous supply and demand expansion (both INDPRO and RSAFS rising >1%), the mechanism does not produce negative 60d returns (IC < 0.05).
